record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Non-product measures still tractable by QSO theory
record.original_question: Find a probability measure μ on the configuration space that is different from the product measure μ(σ) = product_i μ_i(σ_i) in formula (19), but for which the associated non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator can still be analyzed within the framework of the existing theory of quadratic stochastic operators, analogous to how Theorem 11 reduces the product-measure case to separate Volterra QSOs.

evidence.quote: Consider probability measure µ on Ω = Ω1 × . . . × Ωq defined by µ(σ) = ∏_{i=1}^q µi (σi ) ... Theorem 11. [38] The QSO constructed by the construction (18) with respect to measure (19) is reducible to q separate Volterra QSOs.
Problem 18. Find a measure µ different from (19) such that the non-Volterra QSO corresponding to µ can be investigated in the framework of a well known theory of QSOs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $I=\{1,2,\dots,q\}$ be a finite index set, and for each $i\in I$ let $\Omega_i$ be a finite set. Form the configuration space $\Omega=\Omega_1\times\Omega_2\times\cdots\times\Omega_q$ and let $S(\Omega)=\{\lambda:\Omega\to[0,1]\ :\ \sum_{\sigma\in\Omega}\lambda(\sigma)=1\}$ be the simplex of probability measures on $\Omega$.

Given a probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ with $\mu(\sigma)>0$ for all $\sigma\in\Omega$, define the associated quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V_\mu:S(\Omega)\to S(\Omega)$ by
$$
(V_\mu\lambda)(\tau)=\sum_{\sigma,\eta\in\Omega} P_{\sigma,\eta}(\tau)\,\lambda(\sigma)\,\lambda(\eta),\qquad \tau\in\Omega,
$$
where the heredity coefficients $P_{\sigma,\eta}(\tau)\ge 0$ with $\sum_\tau P_{\sigma,\eta}(\tau)=1$ are constructed coordinate-wise from $\mu$ in the standard way: $P_{\sigma,\eta}(\tau)=\mu(\tau)/\bigl(\mu(\sigma)+\mu(\eta)\bigr)$ when $\tau\in\{\sigma,\eta\}$, and $0$ otherwise (with the usual normalisation so that $V_\mu$ is stochastic). A QSO is called Volterra if $P_{\sigma,\eta}(\tau)=0$ whenever $\tau\notin\{\sigma,\eta\}$.

Known fact. If $\mu$ is a product measure, i.e.
$$
\mu(\sigma)=\prod_{i=1}^q\mu_i(\sigma_i),\qquad \sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_q)\in\Omega,\qquad (\star)
$$
for some probability measures $\mu_i$ on $\Omega_i$, then $V_\mu$ decomposes (is reducible) into $q$ independent Volterra QSOs acting on the simplices $S(\Omega_i)$ respectively, and hence its trajectories can be analysed coordinate-wise within the classical theory of Volterra QSOs.

Problem. Exhibit a probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ that is not of the product form $(\star)$ such that the corresponding QSO $V_\mu$ is non-Volterra and yet can be reduced to (or otherwise analysed within) a known, well-developed theory of quadratic stochastic operators (for example, by reduction to a finite collection of Volterra or other tractable QSOs). Equivalently, identify a class of non-product measures $\mu$ on $\Omega$ for which the dynamics of $V_\mu$ on $S(\Omega)$ admits a complete description analogous to the product-measure case.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search shows ongoing activity on non-Volterra QSOs (including those generated by product measures, F-QSOs, permuted Volterra QSOs, and superpositions), but no source directly confirms the discovery of a non-product measure on a general configuration space Ω = Ω₁×···×Ω_q whose induced non-Volterra QSO has been fully analysed within the classical QSO framework in the sense requested. The status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dynamical systems generated by superpositions of extremal Volterra and non-Volterra QSOs on the two-dimensional simplex.
status_evidence.claim: Related research extends QSO theory to certain non-Volterra cases, but does not address the general non-product-measure construction in question.

status_evidence.title: F-quadratic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces F-QSOs as a tractable subclass of QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a tractable subclass but does not solve the problem of identifying non-product measures yielding analyzable non-Volterra QSOs in the stated framework.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic operators corresponding to permutations
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates ongoing extensions of QSO theory but is not a direct resolution of the open problem.
